full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: The plaintiff-respondent filed Title Suit No.58 of 1997 in the Court of Subordinate Judge and First Commercial Court, Dhaka. In that suit, the plaintiff prayed for temporary mandatory injunction for restoration of possession. The trial Court by its Order No. 47 dated 10-7-97 allowed the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction and directed the defendant-petitioner to restore possession of the plaintiff in the suit property within 30 days form the date of order. The defendant-petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned order of the trial Court filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 210 of 1997 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 20-11-97 summarily dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the trial Court. The defendant-petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned judgment of the High Court Division is seeking leave to appeal. 

 2. The plaint case, in short, is that, the suit land originally belonged to one Syed Ali Ahmed, son of late Syed Mohammad Ali. The land was recorded in the name of Syed Ali Ahmed doing the CS operation. The plaintiff took settlement of the said vacant land from the said Syed Ali Ahmed in 1928. It is the case of the plaintiff that he is owning and possessing in some portion of the land and the remaining portion are let out to monthly tenants. There was a dispute between Bhawal Raj Estate Court of Wards and in 1969, the plaintiff paid Taka 55,000.00 to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and in consequence of that the said estate relinquished the claim over the suit property and a deed of compromise was executed by the Manager of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. As the Court of Wards Estate again tried to disturb the plaintiffs possession the suit was filed and injunction was prayed for. On 1-7-93 trial Court directed, the parties to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit property. Notice of this status quo order was served upon the defendant on 1-7-95. In spite of the order of status quo the defendants on 2-7-95 with the help of police forcibly evicted the plaintiff from the suit land. Ultimately, on hearing the parties the learned Subordinate Judge directed the defendants to restore possession of the suit land to the plaintiff. 

 3. Mr Moksudur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division without considering section 18(a) of the Court of Wards Act illegally passed the temporary mandatory injunction directing the defendants to restore possession to the plaintiff and wrongly affirmed the order of the trial Court. 

 4. From the materials on record we find that the learned Judges of the High Court Division found that in spite of service of the order of status quo the defendants willfully evicted the plaintiff from the suit property. The learned Judges also found that Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate filed Title Suit No.395 of 1996 against the plaintiff and his tenants which is still pending. The learned judges of the High Court Division also found that while the civil Court is in section of the matter the defendants could not have taken law in their hands and in that view of the matter affirmed the order of the trial Court granting temporary mandatory injunction. A reference to section 18(a) of the Court of Wards Estate Act shows that this section has no application in the present case as the plaintiff claimed title in the suit property and in case of dispute over the title section 18(a) of the Act has no manner of application. Thus the learned Judges of the High Court Division took a correct view of law and fact in the matter and dismissed the appeal.
